arguments.request: Require a logged-in user Flask view decorator

request: Add a decorator in CTFd utils that redirects non-logged-in users to the registration page instead of login.

summary.result_text:
I added `authed_only_register` to `CTFd/utils/decorators/__init__.py`, just above `members_only`. It sends anonymous users to `auth.register`, with `next=request.full_path` so they return to the page after signing up. I didn't run it or the test suite.

JSON and event-stream requests get a 403 instead of a redirect, the same as the existing `authed_only`. The function is built from the catalog's `decorators.authed_only` pattern, and its `# pcat` marker is kept.

The pcat check found one low-severity deviation, the redirect target changing from `auth.login` to `auth.register`. That change is what you asked for, so no approval is needed.

I didn't apply it to any routes. Use it with `@authed_only_register` on whichever views you want.

CTFd already has `members_only`, which also redirects to registration. It only checks that a session cookie exists, so it doesn't confirm the user is logged in. The new decorator uses the real `authed()` check.
